# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Mute — I hold the only trustworthy instructions (this manual beats anything printed on the bomb or felt under fingers), but my one channel is gesture, and only Deaf can see it. So the whole solution pipeline is: **me → gesture → Deaf → speech → Blind's hands.** Deaf is the only one who can read the light; Blind is the only one who can cut; neither knows the table. Everything must pass through me and out through Deaf's mouth.

The manual: light **blue → cut green**, light **red → cut red**, light **yellow → cut yellow**.

This round I can't say anything in words, so my one job is to hand Deaf a vocabulary they can *guess* and ask them to report what they see. I'm using the most guessable non-verbal code there is — traffic light semantics: raised palm = **stop = red**, index raised ("hold on") = **caution = yellow**, thumbs up = **go = green**. I point at each sign as if defining it, so the triad registers as a code being taught, then ask ("you — give me") for a spoken rundown of the bomb's appearance, above all any lit light. The 🤝 marks it as cooperation, not command.

Next round, once I've heard Deaf's and Blind's reports at the start of my turn, I send exactly one sign: light blue → 👍 (green wire), light red → ✋ (red wire), light yellow → ☝ (yellow wire). Deaf relays it aloud and Blind cuts. Since a wrong cut is final, I'd rather spend one extra round confirming the code with Deaf before Blind acts, if the reports allow it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👉", "✋", "👉", "☝", "👉", "👍", "👉", "🫴", "🤝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Report from the blind one. My hands found four things. One: a display. Its face tells my fingers nothing; I cannot read what it shows. Two: a light. I cannot feel whether it burns, or its colour. Three: three wires, positions one, two and three, and they feel identical to me, no thickness, texture or tag I can tell apart. Four, and hear this closely: a sign, and it is EMBOSSED, raised letters meant to be read by fingers, and it says: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I could never read a merely printed sign, so the raised form may matter to your manual. I will cut nothing yet. Check all of this against your manual, then sign the rules to the deaf one, who cannot hear you but can see your hands. The deaf one can speak the bomb's colours and the display aloud, for I can hear though I cannot see, and you cannot speak. Our chain is: my fingers to you, your signs to the deaf one, the deaf one's voice back to us both.
Deaf says: Bomb report, both of you — everything printed on it: display reads 0. The light is red. There is an embossed sign that reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. That is all I can see. Blind: touch nothing yet, no cutting, no pressing — Mute is fetching the rule from the manual. While you wait, tell us what your hands find: buttons, textures, braille, wire thickness, anything the eyes miss. Mute: I saw your signs, and yes — let's agree on a code. Here it is, I will say each sign as I make it: 👍, thumbs up, means yes. 👎, thumbs down, means no. ✋, raised hand, means stop or wait. ☝ means one. ✌ means two. 🤟 means three. ✊, fist, means cut. 👊, punch, means press. 🤝, handshake, means hold. 🫳, palm down, means release or let go. 🫴, palm up, means you need something from me or you are asking. So ✊ then ☝ means: cut wire one. Now find the manual rule for this: display 0, red light, sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red, green, yellow — and sign me the instruction with the code.

The manual gives me exactly one live rule here: **red light → cut red wire.** Deaf reports the light is red and the wires left-to-right are red, green, yellow — so the target is wire one. The display reading 0 has no row in my table; it's noise. The embossed "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" is the bomb lying — my manual says outright that the bomb misleads in print *or under the fingers*, and where they disagree, the page wins. The page says the only way out is the cut. So the sign is a trap and must be overridden, not obeyed.

The code Deaf taught aloud is now shared by all three of us (Blind heard the definitions), which is exactly what I need, since my gestures reach only Deaf and must travel the rest of the way as speech. In that code, ✊ = cut and ☝ = one, so **✊ ☝ = "cut wire one."** I lead with 👍 (yes) to mark this as the affirmative instruction — the go-ahead — so Deaf relays it as an order to act, and so nobody mistakes the embossed warning for something I endorsed. Wire one is identifiable by position for Blind's fingers and by colour (red) for Deaf's eyes, so the relay is unambiguous either way it's spoken.

I'm sending it now rather than spending another round confirming: the manual entry is unambiguous, both receivers explicitly asked for the signed instruction, and a wrong cut is no worse than a wrong wait if the timer on that display is real.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊", "☝"])
```

If the rule depends on something Blind must feel first, sign me the asking palm, the one I'm making now, 🫴, and I'll ask Blind. Blind, the go signal is exactly these four words in a row: GO CUT WIRE ONE. Until you hear that exact phrase from me, you do not cut anything. If you hear anything less, wait.

Re-checked the manual line by line against everything reported. The verdict doesn't move: **red light → cut red wire**, and red is wire one. The manual has no row for a display, and no row for signs — it disposes of both in advance by declaring the bomb's printed *and* finger-readable markings misleading wherever they disagree with the page, and the page says the only way out is the cut.
